note: Phase 10 source-intelligence research evidence. Nothing in this file grants rights, activates a source, approves a candidate or constitutes a legal conclusion. Every entry needs a named human rights reviewer before any use. An accessible feed is not a republication licence and an API key is not a licence.
method: Official publisher feeds, official API documentation and official licence/terms pages were fetched directly on the access date. Publisher article bodies were not fetched for reuse and no paywall or robots restriction was bypassed.

candidates.name: OSV.dev open-source vulnerability database

evidence.note: The osv.dev infrastructure repository licence was retrieved on the access date: Apache License 2.0, full text.
Official API documentation retrieved on the access date. Documents POST /v1/query, GET /v1/vulns/{id}, querybatch and the OpenSSF Vulnerability data-source model.

verification.licence: Apache-2.0 for the osv.dev infrastructure code
verification.rate_limit: None documented on the public API documentation page retrieved on the access date.
unresolved_legal_questions: The licence retrieved covers the osv.dev infrastructure repository, not automatically the aggregated advisory records it serves. candidates.name: NIST National Vulnerability Database API 2.0
candidates.scope: CVE records with description text, references, weakness identifiers and CVSS vectors. Description text is publisher prose and needs a per-field reuse decision.

evidence.note: Official developer documentation states the public rate limit is 5 requests in a rolling 30 second window and 50 requests in a rolling 30 second window with an API key, and recommends a six second sleep between requests.

verification.rate_limit: 5 requests / 30 s without an API key; 50 requests / 30 s with a key; a six second sleep between requests is recommended.
unresolved_legal_questions: The NVD terms-of-use page did not render retrievable text on the access date, so the reuse grant was not read. It must be read directly before any use.
CVE Program terms of use govern the CVE identifier data inside the NVD records.
Description text reuse is separate from identifier reuse and needs an explicit per-field decision.

candidates.name: CISA cybersecurity advisories feed

evidence.note: Official RSS 2.0 feed retrieved on the access date. It returns advisories with titles, links, dates and full advisory HTML in the description element.

Official CISA terms-of-use page retrieved on the access date. It governs site access, accuracy disclaimers and jurisdiction. It contains no explicit redistribution or republication licence for advisory prose.

verification.rate_limit: None documented; the pipeline applies a bounded fetch policy.

Feed descriptions embed the complete advisory body, so a naive adapter would capture more text than a metadata-only scope permits.
